patch_ledger.before:
Parallel policy evaluation depends on cross-agent correlation, temporal persistence, communication, and update staleness.
We formulate allocation as finite-budget learning-value control: a server selects participation, sample spacing, and step size before an update.
A discrete Lyapunov certificate converts these decisions into a terminal-risk objective for affine delayed temporal-difference learning.
Its terms retain cross-agent second moments, finite-mixing bias, and the delay profile, so the certificate both proves convergence and designs the resource action.
When dependence is unknown, a learning-aware gate purchases a fully charged likelihood probe only when its certified downstream risk reduction exceeds message, transition, delay, and decision-error costs.
We establish a stopped adaptive change-of-measure lower bound, a finite-horizon performance and safety theorem, and a necessary--sufficient budget-threshold sandwich on a separated Markov class.
Controlled studies recover correlation-limited speedup, calibrate the finite-time bounds, and reduce two finite-budget risks by 35.2 and 9.8 percent relative to information-only probing.
patch_ledger.after:
Parallel policy evaluation estimates a common policy's value from multiple Markov trajectories.
Shared disturbances can make additional actors increase communication without providing proportional information.
We develop a finite-budget controller that jointly selects participation, sample spacing, and step size for affine delayed temporal-difference learning.
A discrete Lyapunov bound converts cross-agent second moments, temporal mixing, and update staleness into a terminal-risk score over the affordable learning horizon.
For unknown dependence, a learning-value gate compares the certified benefit of identification with its message, transition, delay, and decision-error costs.
The analysis gives delayed convergence and critic-tracking bounds, a stopped adaptive information lower bound, and a probe-admission rule with certificate-relative risk guarantees.
On a separated Gaussian Markov class, a budget-threshold sandwich links identification feasibility to learning value.
Controlled simulations reduce two finite-budget risks by 35.2 and 9.8 percent relative to information-only probing.

patch_ledger.before:
Held-out multi-agent proximal policy optimization studies on particle coordination and locomotion select dependence-matched participation in all 32 controller runs.
Under identical charged budgets, the controller improves mean normalized team-return curve integrals by 2.32 percent on particles and paired equal-mixture integrals by 8.34 percent on locomotion over the strongest single fixed-participation comparators.
patch_ledger.after:
Held-out cooperative policy-learning studies select dependence-matched participation in all 32 controller runs.
Under identical charged budgets, mean normalized team-return curve integrals improve by 2.32 percent on particles and paired equal-mixture integrals by 8.34 percent on locomotion over the strongest single fixed-participation comparators.

patch_ledger.before:
Temporal-difference and stochastic-approximation foundations~\cite{sutton1988td,tsitsiklis1997td,robbins1951stochastic,polyak1992averaging} lead to finite-time Markov analyses~\cite{bhandari2018finite,srikant2019finite,mou2022optimal}, concentration tools~\cite{paulin2015concentration}, and Lyapunov-based adaptive rates~\cite{gupta2019adaptive}.
Our design also controls the spatial participation and sampling clock creating the observation stream.
patch_ledger.after:
Temporal-difference and stochastic-approximation theory~\cite{sutton1988td,tsitsiklis1997td,robbins1951stochastic,polyak1992averaging} provides finite-time analyses under Markov sampling~\cite{bhandari2018finite,srikant2019finite,mou2022optimal}, concentration bounds~\cite{paulin2015concentration}, and Lyapunov-based adaptive learning rates~\cite{gupta2019adaptive}.
Participation and spacing also determine the observation stream.

patch_ledger.before: Our learning-risk score instead couples cross-agent covariance and Markov spacing to stable step adaptation and the action-dependent number of affordable future updates.
patch_ledger.after: We ask how covariance and spacing change error per update and the number of affordable updates.

patch_ledger.before:
Asynchronous optimization prices stale computation~\cite{agarwal2011distributed,lian2015asynchronous,arjevani2020delayed}; Markov delay-adaptive approximation~\cite{adibi2024delayed,dalfabbro2024dasa} and stochastic delay differential equations (SDDEs) extend convergence and worker-activation design~\cite{yu2025sdde}.
We additionally price the message, transition, and noise cost of correlated trajectories.
patch_ledger.after:
Asynchronous optimization analyzes stale computation~\cite{agarwal2011distributed,lian2015asynchronous,arjevani2020delayed}; delay-adaptive stochastic approximation~\cite{adibi2024delayed,dalfabbro2024dasa} and stochastic delay differential equations (SDDEs) support convergence and worker-activation design~\cite{yu2025sdde}.
Here delay, cross-agent covariance, and paid spacing jointly determine terminal risk.

patch_ledger.before:
Here identification is valued through the remaining learner's risk.
We jointly control these quantities through an action-dependent Lyapunov certificate composed over the affordable updates.
patch_ledger.after:
We value identification through its effect on the remaining learner's risk.
An action-dependent Lyapunov certificate combines the error per update with the number of affordable updates.

patch_ledger.before: \item \textbf{Finite-Budget Learning-Value Formulation:} We jointly control spatial participation, physical Markov spacing, and step size under dual budgets, with an exact correlation-limited Gaussian speedup ceiling.
patch_ledger.after:
\item \textbf{Finite-Budget Lyapunov Resource Design:} A terminal-risk score couples participation, physical Markov spacing, and step size to the number of affordable updates under dual budgets.
The Gaussian resource geometry has an exact correlation-limited speedup ceiling.

patch_ledger.before: \item \textbf{Lyapunov-Certified Resource Control:} An affine delayed Markov certificate supplies the joint score, uniform-history critic tracking, and conservative-certificate risk and selection-sensitivity guarantees.
patch_ledger.after:
\item \textbf{Learning and Certificate Guarantees:} An affine delayed Markov bound supplies the score and a moving-policy critic-tracking guarantee under uniform-history conditions.
Predictable moment/mixing upper bounds control calibration-induced risk and selection error.

patch_ledger.before:
\item \textbf{Charged Learning Evidence:} Controlled studies reduce risk by 35.2 and 9.8 percent relative to information-only probing and held-out parameter/return-estimation area under the curve (AUC) by 9.9/11.3 percent versus a development-selected fixed baseline.
Held-out multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO) studies improve particle mean normalized team-return AUC by 2.32 percent and locomotion paired equal-mixture AUC by 8.34 percent versus the strongest single fixed actions, with all 32 controller runs selecting dependence-matched participation.
patch_ledger.after:
\item \textbf{Resource-Matched Learning Evidence:} Controlled studies quantify the estimation gains from learning-aware probing and finite-horizon control using risk and area under the curve (AUC).
Held-out multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO) studies improve team-return AUC against the strongest single fixed-participation comparators on particles and locomotion, with all 32 controller runs selecting dependence-matched participation.
